newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Samancor sells 50 pct EMSA for 335 mln rand.
newsitem.headline: Samancor sells 50 pct EMSA for 335 mln rand.

text.p: Samancor Ltd said on Wednesday that it had sold its 50 percent interest in graphite electrode manufacturer EMSA to its joint venture partner UCAR International Inc for 335 million rand.

Samancor said in a statement that the proceeds of the sale would offset an expected slump in operating profits and that as a result, second half attributable profits would exceed those of the first half.
In its results for the six months to December 31 last year, the company said it expected results in the second six months to be similar to those in the first half.
"It is now clear that this forecast will not be achieved," it said on Wednesday.

Since December, the rand had strengthened from 4.65 to its current level of 4.44 against the dollar, realised manganese prices had been lower than expected and progress in overcoming production problems at its Metalloys division had been slower than forecast.
"As a consequence of these factors, profit from operations for the second six months of the financial year is now forecast at approximately half of that in the first six months," it said.
At the attributable level, however, the decline in operating profits would be offset by the exceptional profit realised on the sale of the EMSA stake.
"Accordingly second half attributable profits will exceed those of the first half."

Samancor said that EMSA, which also manufactures speciality carbon products, has been managed by UCAR, which is the world's largest producer of graphite and carbon electrodes, and was not a core asset of Samancor.
